steps.what: Hear the emergency alarm and read the room it names
Go to that room and help the person who is there
Tell the nurse what she saw during the response

tasks.design: She hears the emergency on the ward alarm panel in the {OTHER}, goes to that room, and tells the nurse what she saw. The panel names the room. It does not move the patient or decide the response.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right help depends on who is in the room and what she sees when she arrives.
tasks.enabler_now: The panel already names the room. Nothing new replaces going there.
tasks.still_hard: A fire alarm and a medical call can sound alike until she is in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She is the person in the room. The panel cannot help the patient.
tasks.altitude: Answering the alarm and helping in the room stay in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Help her move the patient clear of the alarm
reach.learn: The two-person slide that assistant already uses on this ward

evidence.claim: Going to an alarm and helping the person there is physical work. Model knowledge: a panel that names the room does not do the response.

assumptions: She answers the alarm today, so the actor on every step is the orderly. The machine does not appear in this design.
Telling the nurse what she saw happens in the hospital. It is not a send outside the organisation.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether security calls on this ward are hers or go first to security staff.
research_questions: How often the alarm panel names the right room, and how often she still has to search the corridor?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still hears the emergency, still goes to the room, and still tells the nurse. A quiet shift and a busy one both need her there.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the recipient name on the document before leaving
Carry documents between departments to that named person
Hand the document to that person at the receiving desk

tasks.design: She carries the paper document between departments and hands it to the named person. No copy is made and nothing is sent. A message that is already in the clinical record is not this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: The item is paper that a department still expects in a person's hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new walks a signed paper. The corridor is still the route.
tasks.still_hard: She can read the name and still find the wrong desk in a department she rarely visits.
tasks.human_edge: She holds the paper and puts it in the right person's hand.
tasks.altitude: Walking paper between departments stays in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Take the document she brings to the clinic desk
reach.learn: Which desk in that department accepts the paper

evidence.claim: Carrying a paper document between departments is a walk. Model knowledge: reading the recipient name does not move the paper.

assumptions: She carries the paper today, so the actor on every step is the orderly. The machine does not appear in this design.
Handing the document to a colleague is inside the hospital. It is not a send outside the organisation.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: Which papers this hospital still walks, and which already live only in the clinical record.
research_questions: How often the item is a signed paper, and how often it is a message someone could have sent themselves?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still carries the paper and still hands it over. Days with many signed forms and days with few both keep the walk.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Answer the patient call signal and read the room
Ask that patient at the bedside what they need
Determine whether that need means fetching a nurse
outputs: nurse fetched or simple help given

tasks.design: She answers the patient call on the nurse-call panel in the {OTHER}, goes to the bed, and asks what they need. The light names the room. It does not decide whether a nurse is required.
tasks.previous_blocker: The light does not say whether the patient is in pain, wants water, or cannot breathe.
tasks.enabler_now: The panel already shows the room. The question at the bed stays hers.
tasks.still_hard: A calm request and an urgent one can look the same on the light.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the patient and decides whether to fetch a nurse.
tasks.altitude: Answering the call and asking at the bedside stay in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Hear the need she repeats before a nurse is called
reach.learn: Which stated needs that assistant handles before a nurse comes

evidence.claim: Finding out what a patient needs is a bedside question. Model knowledge: a room light does not say whether the patient can breathe.

assumptions: She answers the call and goes to the bed today, so the actor on every step is the orderly. The machine does not appear in this design.
Telling a nurse the stated need happens in the hospital. It is not a send outside the organisation.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether this ward's call panel already has two-way speech she is allowed to use.
research_questions: How often the stated need is water or a blanket, and how often it is a reason to fetch a nurse at once?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still reads the room, still asks at the bedside, and still decides whether to fetch a nurse. A light that only names the room saves none of that.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week does not change. She still answers alarms, walks paper, and goes to call bells. She gains no new decision right.
skills_to_grow: Say only what she saw at an alarm
Read the recipient on a paper before she walks it
Repeat the patient's words before fetching a nurse
role.ambitious_version: The week does not grow. She does not cover more rooms because an alarm, a paper, or a call signal still needs her there.
